closingRationale: The issue's goal is the v1 skill and both of its open questions were answered by the human before the build: Playwright-only for v1, and standalone with canary-instrument composition documented as optional. All four fault kinds, the seeded reproduction requirement, and the per-flow advisory verdict ship here.
assumptions: Forks answered by the human (CONFIRM, not assumed): Playwright-only for v1; standalone from canary-instrument with composition documented as optional; a seeded reproducible degradation-profile definition shaped so #858's load composer reuses the same vocabulary; output is an advisory per-flow verdict, not a gate.

harness:brainstorming ran in autonomous mode (recommended defaults, no waiting) and produced the proposal; harness:autopilot's PLAN/EXECUTE stages ran as planning + TDD here, and VERIFY/INTEGRATE were replaced by the agents/skills gates (test/typecheck/format:check), the ts/ four gates, and the four CI ratchets measured locally against origin/main.

D5 (lane assumption): the injection decision is keyed by request IDENTITY (seed | fault id | METHOD url#ordinal-within-flow), never by arrival order, so a parallel run is reproducible. Consequence, stated in SKILL.md: changing how many times a flow calls a URL changes its decisions at the same seed.
D6 (lane assumption): a skill only, no ts/ CLI subcommand and no domain-registry entry — nothing here needs the engine, matching canary-screech/fail-fast/katana.
D8 (lane assumption): a passing flow is `degraded` when it retried or exceeded budget_ms; absent a stated budget, twice the injected delay; absent both, an unstated budget is never breached.

The shipped Playwright route fixture is NOT executed by this repo's CI — Playwright is not a canary dependency and no browser is installed. It is verified through its pure decision engine and a fake route/request double, and excluded from the coverage gate exactly as canary-instrument's OTel bootstrap is. This is the one place the spike could not confirm a live browser run.

Spike finding (T0): the complexity analyzer's brace counter is blinded by a literal open-brace inside a string literal — `text.indexOf('{')` made a 20-line function measure as '90 lines, complexity 21' and failed the unwaivable perf delta rule. Worked around with a String.fromCharCode(123) constant and a comment; canary-fail-fast's parse.mjs has the same shape and is grandfathered into the absolute baseline (not fixed here — out of scope).

Ratchets measured locally against origin/main with harness CLI 12.9.0: entropy 144 -> 144 (delta 0); perf 219 -> 220, the one new finding allowed by the existing `coupling agents/skills/claude-code/*/scripts/cli.mjs` allowance, 0 blocking, baseline 233; docs 30/278 -> 30/284, no link lost; check-deps and validate pass.

PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here: `harness check-arch` reports a BASELINE TRIP (0 new violations, 12 pre-existing) IDENTICALLY on origin/main measured in a clean worktree, so .harness/arch/baselines.json is stale relative to main. This lane did not refresh the baseline or write an allowance for someone else's drift.

All five new .mjs modules are declared in BOTH harness.config.json entryPoints arrays; agents/skills/package.json format glob and vitest coverage include were extended (top-level scripts only, so the route fixture stays out of the coverage gate).
